questions.ref: Network Theorems For DC & Miscellaneous Topics Q3
questions.question: Superposition theorem does not hold for
options: networks containing diodes and R-C element
questions.explanation:
Superposition theorem is not applicable to networks containing non-linear elements such as diodes. The Superposition theorem is applicable to :
  1. Linear networks.
  2. Time-variant or time-invariant networks.
  3. Networks containing independent sources.
  4. Networks containing linear dependent sources (voltage or current).
  5. Networks containing linear passive elements \(R\), \(L\), \(C\) and linear transformers.
  6. Networks containing different frequency sources.
(B) networks containing diodes and R-C element
Key points
  • Superposition theorem is applicable only to linear networks.
  • It is not applicable to circuits containing non-linear elements such as diodes, transistors operating in non-linear regions, etc.
  • Superposition can be used in networks containing both independent and linear dependent sources.

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: For a sinusoidal input of \(50\text{ V}\) amplitude, the circuit shown in figure can be used as
questions.explanation: The two Zener diodes are connected back-to-back, forming a symmetrical voltage limiter. When \(V_i>5~\text{V},\) one Zener diode operates in breakdown while the other is forward biased. Hence, \(V_o\approx5~\text{V}.\) Similarly, when \(V_i<-5~\text{V},\) the other Zener diode goes into breakdown and \[\Rightarrow V_o\approx-5~\text{V}.\] Thus, the output is clipped at \(\pm5~\text{V}.\) For a sinusoidal input of amplitude \(50~\text{V}\), the output waveform is clipped at \(\pm5~\text{V}\), resulting in a waveform that closely resembles a square wave. Hence, the circuit acts as a \[\boxed{\textbf{B. }\text{Square Wave Generator}}\]

From the table, choose the correct logical expression for \(Q\):
\(A\)00001111
\(B\)00110011
\(C\)01010101
\(Q\)00010111
questions.explanation:
From the given table, the canonical SOP form is: \[Q = \bar ABC + A \bar BC + AB \bar C + ABC\]
Method 1
Simplifying, we get: \[Q = AB ( \bar C+C) + BC ( \bar A+A) +CA ( \bar B+B) = AB+BC+CA\]
Method 2
Simplifying, we get: \[Q = AB ( \bar C+C) + \bar ABC + A \bar BC = AB +\bar ABC + A \bar BC\] \[Q = A( \bar BC+B) + \bar ABC = AB + AC + \bar ABC\] \[Q = B(A+\bar AC) + AC = AB +BC+CA\]
Method 3
K-Map can be drawn as: The obtained SOP expression is \[Q =AB + BC +AC\]
\[\boxed{(A)\;AB+BC+CA}\]

questions.question: For an 8085 microprocessor, the Stack Pointer (SP) and Program Counter (PC) registers contain the number F000 and 2400 in Hex respectively. The contents of the register after execution of the instruction CALL E000 would be
questions.explanation: Given: \(SP = F000,\text{H}\), \(PC = 2400,\text{H}\). If the CALL E000H instruction is executed, the current contents of the program counter are pushed onto the top of the stack, and the program counter is initialized with \(E000,\text{H}\). Due to the pushing operation, the contents of the stack pointer are decremented by 2. \[PC = E000,\text{H}\] \[SP = 23FE,\text{H}\] \[\boxed{(D) \text{ PC : E000 , SP : 23 FE}}\]

questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.question: Indicate which one of the following statements is correct.
options: Static RAMs are faster than dynamic RAMs
RAMs cannot be used to realise Read Write Memory (RWM)
ROMs are not random access devices
questions.explanation: This question evaluates statements regarding RAM and ROM memory devices. Option (A): Static RAM uses a completely different technology compared to dynamic RAM. In static RAM, a form of flip-flop holds each bit of memory. A flip-flop memory cell takes 4 to 6 transistors along with some wiring, but it never has to be refreshed. This makes static RAM significantly faster than dynamic RAM. Hence, option (A) is correct. Option (B): RAM can be used to realize Read Write Memory (RWM). Hence, option (B) is incorrect (the statement itself is true, but it is not the intended answer). Option (C): ROM is stated to be a type of Random Access Device. Hence, option (C) is incorrect. Option (D): RAM comes under the category of volatile memory. Hence, option (D) is incorrect. Hence, the correct option is (A). \[\boxed{(A) \text{ Static RAMs are faster than dynamic RAMs}}\]

questions.question:
Find the correct match among the following pairs in the context of an 8085 microprocessor.
(a)DAA;;;;(e)Program control instruction
(b)LXI;;;;(f)Data movement instruction
(c)RST;;;;(g)Interrupt instruction
(d)JMP;;;;(h)Arithmetic
questions.explanation: This is a matching-type question pairing 8085 instructions with their classification/description. (a) DAA: The contents of the accumulator are changed from a binary value to two 4-bit Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) digits. It is an arithmetic instruction. a \(\rightarrow\)(h) (b) LXI (Load Register Pair Immediate): This instruction loads 16-bit data into the register pair designated in the operand. It is a data movement instruction. b \(\rightarrow\) (f) (c) RST: It is basically a quick subroutine call to one of 8 predefined addresses (\(0\text{X}00, 0\text{X}08, 0\text{X}10, 0\text{X}18, 0\text{X}20, 0\text{X}28, 0\text{X}38\)). It is a type of software interrupt instruction. c \(\rightarrow\) (g) (d) JUMP: It is a branch control or program control instruction. d \(\rightarrow\) (e) \[\boxed{(B) \text{ a-h, b-f, c-g, d-e}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.ref: Block Diagram and Signal Flow Graph Q1
questions.question:
Common Data for Q2.00.1 and Q2.00.2. Fig. shows the block diagram for a system with feed forward control.

Find the transfer function between the output \(y\) and the disturbance input \(w\).
questions.note: No single correct answer in the official key
questions.explanation:
With \(u(s) = 0\), considering \(w(s)\) as the input and \(y(s)\) as the output:
  • Forward Paths: \(P_1 = G_p(s)\) and \(P_2 = G_f(s)G_c(s)G_p(s)\)
  • Individual Loops: \(L_1 = -G_c(s)G_p(s)H(s)\)
  • Path Determinants: Since the loop touches both forward paths, \(\Delta_1 = 1\) and \(\Delta_2 = 1\).
  • System Determinant: \(\Delta = 1 - L_1 = 1 + G_c(s)G_p(s)H(s)\).
Applying Mason's Gain Formula: \(\dfrac{Y(s)}{W(s)} = \dfrac{\sum P_i\Delta_i}{\Delta}\): \[\frac{Y(s)}{W(s)} = \frac{G_p(s) + G_f(s)G_c(s)G_p(s)}{1 + G_c(s)G_p(s)H(s)}\] \[\boxed{\frac{Y(s)}{W(s)} = \frac{G_p(s)\left[1 + G_c(s)G_f(s)\right]}{1 + G_c(s)G_p(s)H(s)}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.ref: Block Diagram and Signal Flow Graph Q2
questions.question:
Common Data for Q2.00.1 and Q2.00.2. Fig. shows the block diagram for a system with feed forward control.

What would be the transfer function of the feed forward controller \(G_f(s)\) to eliminate completely the effect of the disturbance input \(w\)?
questions.note: No single correct answer in the official key
questions.explanation:
To achieve complete isolation or absolute tracking rejection against incoming load fluctuations, the output \(y(s)\) must remain invariant to \(w(s)\): \[\frac{Y(s)}{W(s)} = 0\] Since the characteristic polynomial denominator governs absolute loop stability metrics, it cannot be rendered infinite. Thus, set the open-loop numerator term identically to zero: \[1 + G_c(s)G_f(s) = 0\] \[\boxed{G_f(s) = -\frac{1}{G_c(s)}}\]
Key points
  • Feedforward Inversion: The ideal feedforward controller acts as the structural inverse of the feedback control block to cancel paths before errors propagate through the plant.
  • Superposition Principle: Linear systems allow individual inputs to be analyzed independently by nulling all secondary independent sources.

questions.question: For a unity feedback system with open loop transfer function \(G(s) = \dfrac{9}{s(s + 2)}\), the damping ratio is
questions.explanation: The closed-loop transfer function (T.F.) is : \[T(s) = \frac{\dfrac{9}{s(s+2)}}{1 + \dfrac{9}{s(s+2)}} = \frac{9}{s(s+2) + 9} = \frac{9}{s^2 + 2s + 9}\] Comparing the characteristic equation \(s^2 + 2s + 9 = 0\) with the standard second-order characteristic equation \(s^2 + 2\zeta\omega_n s + \omega_n^2 = 0\): \[\omega_n^2 = 9 \implies \omega_n = 3\] \[2\zeta\omega_n = 2 \implies 2\zeta \times 3 = 2 \implies \zeta = \frac{1}{3}\] \[\boxed{(A) \ \ \frac{1}{3}}\]

questions.question: The asymptotic Bode plot for the gain magnitude of a minimum phase system \(G(s)\) is shown below The transfer function is \(G(s)=\)
questions.explanation:
From the asymptotic Bode magnitude plot:
  • Initial slope is \(0\,\text{dB/decade}\) \(\Rightarrow\) no pole or zero at the origin.
  • The slope changes from \(0\) to \(-20\,\text{dB/decade}\) at \(\omega=10\,\text{rad/s}\), indicating a pole at \(10\,\text{rad/s}\).
  • The slope changes from \(-20\) to \(-40\,\text{dB/decade}\) at \(\omega=250\,\text{rad/s}\), indicating another pole at \(250\,\text{rad/s}\).
Hence, \[G(s)=\frac{K}{(1+s/10)(1+s/250)}\] The low-frequency gain is \(40\,\text{dB}\). Hence, \[20\log_{10}K=40\] \[K=10^{40/20}=100\] Therefore, \[G(s)=\frac{100}{(1+s/10)(1+s/250)}\] \[\boxed{(A)\;\dfrac{100}{(1+s/10)(1+s/250)}}\]

questions.question: The proportional gain of a PID controller can be expressed in terms of its proportional band (PB) as
questions.explanation:
The proportional band (PB) and proportional gain (\(K_p\)) are related by \[\mathrm{PB}=\frac{100}{K_p}\] \[K_p=\frac{100}{\mathrm{PB}}\] Therefore, the proportional gain is: \[\boxed{(B)\;\dfrac{100}{\mathrm{PB}}}\]
Key points
  • Proportional band and proportional gain are inversely proportional.
  • Increasing proportional gain decreases the proportional band.

Consider the plant shown in the below figure with a proportional controller with a positive gain.. \[\QuestionFigureNoNumber[width=1\columnwidth]{img/ch10_controllers_and_compensators/Q10_00_2.png}\]

The open loop step response of the plant is:
questions.explanation: The plant consists of two first-order systems connected in parallel. Hence, \[G_p(s)=\frac{2}{1+0.5s}-\frac{1}{1+0.1s}\] The overall open loop transfer function will be, \[\frac{Y(s)}{R(s)} = KG_p(s) = K\left[\frac{-6s+20}{(s+2)(s+10)}\right]\] For a unit step input, \(R(s)=\dfrac{1}{s}\) \[Y(s)=\frac{1}{s} \times K\left[\frac{-6s+20}{(s+2)(s+10)}\right]\] \[Y(s)= K\left[\frac{-6s+20}{s(s+2)(s+10)}\right]\] \[Y(s)= K\left[\frac{1}{s}-\frac{2}{s+2}+\frac{1}{s+10}\right]\] Taking Inverse Laplace transform, \[y(t) = K\left[1-2e^{-2t}+e^{-10t} \right]\] For: \[t=0 \qquad y(t)=0\] \[t=1 \qquad y(t)=0.26K\] \[t=\infty \qquad y(t)=K\] Thus, the open-loop step response starts from zero and asymptotically approaches a constant value (K) without overshoot or oscillation. Hence, the correct option is: \[\boxed{(C)}\]
